pathway.title: PBF Holding Co LLC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Liquidity and low leverage are the main support, and no drawn debt falls due before 2032 once the October redemption is counted. Debt was 0.40x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 6.90x at FY2025, cash interest was covered 25.09x against 2.05x, and revolver availability was about USD 3,100.0 million after the commitment was raised to USD 4.0 billion and extended to 2031-09-30. After the October redemption USD 1,050.0 million of notes remain, due in 2032 and 2034. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation CB1; calculation CB3; calculation CB9

- Earnings are the weak point because they follow the refining cycle. EBITDA excluding special items was negative USD 124.2 million in FY2024 and negative USD 9.5 million in FY2025, when gross refining margin was USD 7.89 and USD 8.77 per barrel, against USD 3,259.1 million for the first nine months of 2026 at USD 22.96 per barrel. Each USD 1.00 per barrel of margin is worth about USD 304.0 million a year at FY2025 volumes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation CB4

- Cash flow in 2026 is strong but not all earned. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 3,070.6 million and capital spending USD 933.8 million, but accrued expenses added USD 981.1 million while receivables absorbed USD 904.3 million and inventories USD 339.0 million. Inventory-related accruals rose to USD 2,378.3 million from USD 1,351.5 million at 2025-12-31 and the filings do not say what they are owed to, and USD 102.9 million of operating cash flow was insurance proceeds. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation CB8

- Refinancing risk is low until 2032, but market access has been shown at the top of the cycle and at a high price in the trough. The 2034 notes of USD 500.0 million at 7.25% and the 2032 exchangeable notes of USD 550.0 million were placed in 2026, and annual cash coupons fell from about USD 166.5 million to USD 36.25 million, yet in March 2025, a loss year, the issuer paid a coupon close to ten percent to place USD 800.0 million of 2030 notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17-18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21-22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation CB10

- Margin resilience is weak because product and crude prices are set by the market and regulatory cost is large. Renewable fuel compliance cost rose to USD 1,132.1 million for nine months from USD 454.0 million, though it took 19.31% of reported gross refining margin against 25.90% a year earlier, and a change of USD 1.00 per MMBTU in natural gas moves annual energy cost by USD 70.0 million to USD 100.0 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation CB12; calculation CB15

- Capital spending is the main lever in a downturn, and it has limits. Turnarounds were 32.68% of nine-month capital spending, the 2026 guidance is USD 825.0 million to USD 875.0 million excluding the Martinez rebuild with two turnarounds moved to 2027, and FY2025 spending was USD 1,144.0 million; deferring maintenance saves cash but raises outage risk at a system with one reportable segment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66-67; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156; calculation CB8; calculation CB13

- Structure and the parent are a second downside channel. The notes rank behind a USD 4.0 billion secured revolver and behind subsidiaries that do not guarantee them, and net cash flows to the parent were outflows of USD 424.0 million in FY2023 and USD 306.0 million in FY2024 before turning into net contributions of USD 199.6 million in FY2025 and USD 29.6 million in the first nine months of 2026; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation CB11

- Event risk and information gaps cap confidence. Penalties from the Martinez fire investigations are unknown although insurers have paid USD 1.25 billion, the effect of the Chalmette fire of 2026-05-08 is not stated, and no current ratings, peer data, covenant calculations or management forecast are supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75

runs.text: The main strengths are liquidity, distant and cheaper debt, scale, recovered interest cover and insurance recoveries already received. Net cash and about USD 3,100.0 million of revolver availability sit against USD 1,050.0 million of notes due in 2032 and 2034 after the October redemption, and annual cash coupons fell by about USD 130.2 million; the issuer runs six refineries in four regions with a weighted-average Nelson Complexity Index of 12.8; interest cover was 25.09x; and insurers have paid USD 1.25 billion of the Martinez claim, which management expects to finalise before year-end 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation CB1; calculation CB9; calculation CB10

The main weaknesses are cyclical earnings, cash-flow quality, regulatory cost, cash calls from the parent and ranking. EBITDA excluding special items was negative in FY2024 and FY2025; 2026 operating cash flow leans on accruals and insurance; renewable fuel compliance cost reached USD 1,132.1 million for nine months; parent distributions were USD 156.4 million for nine months with an 18% dividend increase declared; and the notes sit behind a USD 4.0 billion secured revolver and non-guarantor subsidiaries. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation CB4; calculation CB8

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Between May and October 2026 the issuer issued USD 500.0 million of 7.25% senior unsecured notes due 2034 and USD 550.0 million of 0.00% exchangeable senior notes due 2032, and redeemed its 2028 notes and both 2030 note series. The 2034 notes were issued on 2026-05-28 for net proceeds of USD 492.1 million and, with cash, funded the redemption at par of USD 801.6 million of 6.00% notes on 2026-06-25. The 2032 exchangeable notes were issued on 2026-09-17 for net proceeds of USD 533.2 million, of which USD 27.7 million paid for capped call transactions; the remainder and cash redeemed USD 500.0 million of 7.875% notes on 2026-09-24 at 103.938% of principal. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21-24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37-38

The 2032 exchangeable notes carry no regular interest, mature on 2032-01-15 and are exchangeable into PBF Energy Class A shares at an initial exchange price of about USD 96.80, with settlement in cash up to principal. PBF Energy is a party to the indenture, the registration rights agreement and the capped calls, and the notes are guaranteed by certain issuer subsidiaries. The filing does not say whether PBF Energy guarantees the notes. The 2034 notes are senior unsecured, guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, rank equal in right of payment with the revolver and are effectively subordinated to secured debt including the revolver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18-22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 83

On 2026-09-30 the issuer amended and restated its asset-based revolver, extending maturity to 2031-09-30, raising the commitment from USD 3.5 billion to USD 4.0 billion and cutting the commitment fee on the unused portion. On 2026-09-09 PBF Energy Company LLC closed the purchase of two hydrogen plants at the Torrance refinery from Air Products and contributed them to the issuer, which recognised USD 388.4 million of property, plant and equipment and removed an operating lease liability of USD 139.7 million and a right-of-use asset of USD 140.2 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13-14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

After the balance-sheet date, on 2026-10-26, the issuer redeemed all USD 800.0 million of its 9.875% notes due 2030 at 106.67% of principal, about USD 853.4 million, from cash on hand; a loss of USD 70.4 million is to be booked in Q4 2026. PBF Energy declared a dividend of USD 0.325 per share on 2026-10-29, payable on 2026-11-24, and the issuer may need to distribute cash to PBF Energy Company LLC to fund it. PBF Energy must file a resale registration statement for the exchange shares by 2026-12-31 or special interest of 0.25% to 0.50% a year accrues. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68

fields.value: PBF Holding Co LLC (issuer id pbf-holding-co-llc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: the issuer's own statements, net debt, leverage, coverage, liquidity and debt maturities from the 2025 annual report and the three 2026 quarterly reports, with the parent's earnings releases as context only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PBF Holding ended Q3 2026 in net cash of USD 897.6 million with debt at 0.40x LTM EBITDA, so near-term leverage risk is low, but the ratio rests on a refining upswing and insurance gains, as FY2025 EBITDA was only USD 311.3 million. Net debt was USD 1,645.3 million, or 5.29x EBITDA, at the end of FY2025 after negative EBITDA in FY2024, so leverage can reverse quickly if margins fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C24; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the October 2026 redemption of the last of the 2030 senior notes, net cash is about USD 827.2 million and no drawn debt matures before 2032. The reported debt figure is a carrying value that sits below principal, and the parent's own debt figure for the same date is higher and not reconciled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_a991pressreleaseq3-26.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage fell from stress to negligible in three quarters because debt was repaid while earnings recovered: debt was USD 2,802.3 million at 2026-03-31 against LTM EBITDA of USD 1,089.4 million, or 2.57x, and USD 1,613.0 million against USD 4,072.7 million, or 0.40x, at 2026-09-30. LTM EBITDA covered cash interest 25.09x against 2.05x in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_pbf-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C25; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings behind that ratio are cyclical and partly non-recurring, which is the main reason to hold the conclusion loosely: FY2024 EBITDA was negative USD 245.4 million, FY2025 EBITDA of USD 311.3 million included an insurance gain of USD 832.5 million and was negative USD 9.5 million before special items, and the first nine months of 2026 include an insurance gain of USD 356.5 million. The issuer's adjusted LTM EBITDA is USD 3,505.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating cash flow was lifted by growth in accrued liabilities, not only by profit: in the nine months of 2026 operating cash flow was USD 3,070.6 million after accrued expenses added USD 981.1 million while receivables absorbed USD 904.3 million and inventories USD 339.0 million. Inventory-related accruals were USD 2,378.3 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 1,351.5 million at 2025-12-31, and the filings do not say what they are owed to, so a reversal would draw on the cash balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is ample: cash was USD 2,510.6 million and revolver availability about USD 3,100.0 million at 2026-09-30, after the revolver was extended to 2031-09-30 and enlarged to USD 4,000.0 million. The issuer states availability only as an approximate figure, and letters of credit outstanding were about USD 157.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity wall is distant: the debt table at 2026-09-30 lists USD 800.0 million due in 2030, USD 550.0 million of exchangeable notes due in 2032 and USD 500.0 million due in 2034, with the revolver undrawn. The 2030 notes were redeemed on 2026-10-26 for about USD 853.4 million, which leaves pro forma net cash of USD 827.2 million, or 0.20x EBITDA, before accrued interest on the redemption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported debt understates the contractual claim: principal at 2026-09-30 was USD 1,850.0 million against a carrying value of USD 1,613.0 million, mostly a USD 174.0 million discount created when the exchange feature of the 2032 notes was valued separately as a liability of USD 197.6 million, which sits outside the debt line. Leverage on principal is 0.45x.

fields.value: The stack shows principal, not carrying value, and the 2030 notes were redeemed after the balance sheet date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge uses the issuer's own add-backs for the nine months to 2026-09-30 and none is a plug.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer reports one segment, Refining, which includes its six refineries, so segment revenue equals consolidated revenue and no segment schedule or eliminations row is stated. Subsequent events after 2026-09-30 are the redemption of the 2030 senior notes on 2026-10-26 and the parent's dividend declared on 2026-10-29 and payable 2026-11-24; they are kept out of every period figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All amounts are USD million unless a ratio is shown in times; a negative net debt is net cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The parent's Q3 2026 release reports total debt of USD 2,118.4 million while the issuer's balance sheet shows long-term debt of USD 1,613.0 million at 2026-09-30, and no supplied document bridges the USD 505.4 million difference; every ratio here uses the issuer's figure, so the parent's debt perimeter is not measured. Severity Medium; the action that would close it is a bridge from the issuer or the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Statement lines that the filings print as a dash, such as the gain on insurance recoveries in FY2024 and the loss on extinguishment of debt in several periods, are written as not supplied and are not read as zero; a line that a document does not print at all, such as the 2034 notes proceeds before the first half of 2026, is marked in the same way. This restricts only sums that include those lines, which the statement identities do not need. Severity Low; no action is needed beyond reading the cells as nil lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revolver availability is stated by the issuer only as an approximate or more-than figure for 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-30 and is not split out for 2024-12-31, so the liquidity chart carries rounded availability and one gap. This restricts precise liquidity and borrowing-base analysis. Severity Low; the action is the borrowing base certificate or the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is built from the instrument list because the quarterly reports print no maturity table, and the maturity days of the 2030 and 2034 notes are not stated. This restricts the timing of the 2034 and 2030 maturities to the year. Severity Low; the action is the indentures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is printed net of capitalised interest and gross cash interest is not restated, so coverage in every period is higher than it would be on gross interest. This restricts the interest cover figures. Severity Low; the action is the capitalised interest by period, which the filings print.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The settlement of the hydrogen plants purchase, including the secured promissory note the second-quarter report said would be issued by the parent, is not described in the Q3 2026 statements, so any related obligation outside the issuer's debt line is not established. This restricts claims outside debt. Severity Medium; the action is the closing terms of the purchase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No balance sheet at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 or 2025-09-30 is supplied, so period-end debt and cash for those dates are not stated and the leverage trend begins at 2024-12-31. This restricts prior-year quarterly comparison of net debt. Severity Low; the action is the 2025 quarterly reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The accrued expenses line includes inventory-related accruals of USD 2,378.3 million at 2026-09-30, and the filings do not say who they are owed to or when they settle, so the cash effect of a reversal is not established. This restricts the quality of operating cash flow and liquidity. Severity Medium; the action is the accrual composition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Insurance premium financing is shown in the cash flow statement but its outstanding balance is not identified in the debt note, so it is not in Total Debt and its size at 2026-09-30 is not established. Severity Low; the action is the balance and the lender terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma net debt after the 2026-10-26 redemption excludes accrued interest paid on the redemption date, and the issuer's cash distribution to its parent for the dividend payable 2026-11-24 is not stated, so no effect is worked for it. Severity Low; the action is the cash paid at redemption and the distribution amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - FY2023 income and cash flow statements are printed in the annual report but are not carried here because no ratio uses them. Severity Low; the action is to add them if a three-year trend is wanted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PBF Holding Co LLC (issuer id pbf-holding-co-llc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: the issuer's business, transactions, ownership and operating model and the governance and sponsor behaviour that bear on its creditors, read from the seven supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PBF Holding is the six-refinery operating subsidiary of a listed parent, and sponsor and governance risk for its creditors is medium: the parent has put capital and assets into the issuer in 2026, but it can draw distributions and its executives run the issuer. Cash flow between issuer and parent was a net outflow of USD 306.0 million in FY2024, a loss year, and became a net inflow of USD 199.6 million in FY2025 and USD 29.6 million in the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No executed debt documents were supplied, so the limits on distributions rest on the filings' summaries. The 2026 refinancings paid noteholders in full or at a premium, with no exchange, uptier or drop-down documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CA4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control is complete and internal, so creditors cannot count on an independent board or an outside sponsor to restrain distributions. PBF Energy Company LLC owns all of the issuer, PBF Energy Inc. holds about 99.3% of the economic interests in that company, and the issuer's three directors are executives of the parent who receive no separate pay. The documents name no financial sponsor, so fund life and exit pressure do not apply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Distributions to the parent are a recurring route for value to leave the issuer, and they continued through a loss year. Distributions less capital contributions were a net outflow of USD 424.0 million in FY2023, with USD 853.4 million of assets also distributed, and USD 306.0 million in FY2024, when the issuer lost USD 895.9 million. The flow reversed to a net contribution of USD 199.6 million in FY2025 and USD 29.6 million in the first nine months of 2026. In FY2025 the issuer distributed USD 273.1 million, of which USD 126.5 million was passed on as non-tax distributions to members, USD 125.6 million of it to the parent for its dividends, and the filing does not trace the other USD 146.6 million. USD 119.9 million of the USD 156.4 million distributed in the first nine months of 2026 fell in Q3. The indentures also let the issuer distribute enough for the parent to meet its tax receivable agreement payments, which the filing says could be significant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93-94; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 154-156; 10-Q_2026-06-30_pbf-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9-10; calculation CA1; calculation CA2; calculation CA3; calculation CA13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The parent's 2026 support is real but mostly non-cash, and its terms are incomplete. Capital contributions of USD 186.0 million and the hydrogen plants contributed at USD 388.4 million exceed distributions of USD 156.4 million, but the second-quarter report described a secured promissory note of USD 320.0 million to USD 340.0 million to be issued by the parent on closing, and the third-quarter report does not say whether any claim attaches to plants now held by the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing behaviour in 2026 was creditor-aligned in form, with no restructuring tactic documented. The 2028 notes were redeemed at par for USD 801.6 million, and both 2030 series were redeemed at premiums of about USD 19.7 million and USD 53.4 million, funded from new unsecured notes and cash. The supplied filings record no exchange, uptier, priming, drop-down or waiver, which is a finding about what is documented and not proof that none occurred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23-24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CA4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ranking is the main structural weakness: the notes are senior unsecured, equal to the secured revolver only in right of payment, and sit behind its collateral and behind subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. The revolver commitment was raised by USD 500.0 million to USD 4.0 billion on 2026-09-30, was undrawn at the quarter end, and had letters of credit of about USD 157.2 million outstanding. Eleven named subsidiaries guarantee the notes, but the guarantor group's nine-month net income of USD 4,911.2 million is USD 1,641.6 million above the consolidated USD 3,269.6 million and the filing does not reconcile the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22-24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 69-70; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 181; calculation CA5; calculation CA6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Related-party dependence is material and rising. Purchases from the affiliate SBR were USD 788.7 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 313.8 million a year earlier, or 3.05% of cost of products; expenses under agreements with the affiliate PBFX, which owns logistics assets the issuer once held, were USD 270.4 million; and the issuer guarantees up to 50% of a USD 100.0 million SBR term loan, a risk it calls remote.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24-26; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 24-26; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 182; calculation CA7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are a refining-margin credit, concentrated in one reportable segment of six refineries with about one million barrels a day of capacity. Gasoline and distillates were 88.82% of nine-month revenues of USD 31,703.8 million, gross refining margin excluding special items was USD 22.96 per barrel against USD 7.89, and the cost of renewable-fuel compliance rose to USD 1,132.1 million from USD 454.0 million, though it took 19.31% of reported gross refining margin against 25.90% a year earlier. Customer concentration is moderate, with one customer at about 13% of FY2025 revenues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Event risk is unquantified rather than absent. Investigations into the Martinez fire and a 2022 catalyst release carry no stated penalty, although insurers have paid USD 1.25 billion and the claim is expected to be finalised before year-end 2026. The Chalmette fire of 2026-05-08 is named only as a risk with no stated cost, while Gulf Coast throughput in Q3 2026 was 3.84% lower than a year earlier and 22 notices of violation relate to the Martinez fire.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation CA10; calculation CA11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure supports monitoring of reported results but not of restrictions. The issuer files full annual and quarterly reports as a voluntary filer, the FY2025 audit opinion is unmodified and disclosure controls were effective at 2026-09-30, but the executed debt documents, covenant certificates, basket usage and current ratings are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for lower risk is that the parent has been a net provider of capital since FY2025, that the filings document no waiver, amendment of note terms or non-pro-rata transaction, that USD 800.0 million of 2030 notes were redeemed at a premium in October 2026 from cash, and that earnings recovered sharply, with net income of USD 1,906.0 million in Q3 2026. The assessment would move to low if the executed documents show tight restricted-payment capacity and the next two quarters show distributions no larger than the parent's dividend need.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 155-156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CA1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for higher risk is the pattern of FY2023 and FY2024, with net outflows of USD 424.0 million and USD 306.0 million and assets of USD 853.4 million distributed, the stated practice of distributing to fund more than one year of the parent's dividends, the 18% dividend increase, and the fact that 76.7% of nine-month distributions fell in Q3 2026, the quarter with net income of USD 1,906.0 million. A distribution above the dividend need, a revolver draw that funds shareholder payments, or a call on the SBR loan guarantee would move the assessment to high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 155-156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 68-69; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_a991pressreleaseq3-26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation CA1; calculation CA12; calculation CA13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed indentures and the amended revolving credit agreement are not supplied, so the conclusion that distributions are limited by incurrence tests and default blocks rests on the filings' own summaries; wider restricted-payment capacity in the documents would raise the sponsor risk assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The parent's proxy statement, which carries its board, committees and holders, is incorporated by reference and not supplied, so the conclusion on control and board independence stops at the issuer's three directors; independent oversight at the parent could lower the risk assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings trace the use of distributions only for FY2025, so the reading of distributions as parent dividend funding is untested for FY2023, FY2024 and 2026; a use other than dividends and tax payments would raise the assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The hydrogen plants terms, the Chalmette fire effect and the Martinez penalties are not quantified, so the support and event-risk conclusions are bounded; a promissory note secured on the plants would cut the value of the parent's 2026 support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The difference between guarantor-group and consolidated earnings is not reconciled, so how much value sits behind the guarantees is not established and the ranking conclusion could be better or worse than stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Between May and October 2026 the issuer issued USD 500.0 million of 7.25% senior unsecured notes due 2034 and USD 550.0 million of 0.00% exchangeable senior notes due 2032, and redeemed its 2028 notes and both 2030 note series. The 2034 notes were issued on 2026-05-28 for net proceeds of USD 492.1 million and, with cash, funded the redemption at par of USD 801.6 million of 6.00% notes on 2026-06-25. The 2032 exchangeable notes were issued on 2026-09-17 for net proceeds of USD 533.2 million, of which USD 27.7 million paid for capped call transactions; the remainder and cash redeemed USD 500.0 million of 7.875% notes on 2026-09-24 at 103.938% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2032 exchangeable notes carry no regular interest, mature on 2032-01-15 and are exchangeable into PBF Energy Class A shares at an initial exchange price of about USD 96.80, with settlement in cash up to principal. PBF Energy is a party to the indenture, the registration rights agreement and the capped calls, and the notes are guaranteed by certain issuer subsidiaries. The filing does not say whether PBF Energy guarantees the notes. The 2034 notes are senior unsecured, guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, rank equal in right of payment with the revolver and are effectively subordinated to secured debt including the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-09-30 the issuer amended and restated its asset-based revolver, extending maturity to 2031-09-30, raising the commitment from USD 3.5 billion to USD 4.0 billion and cutting the commitment fee on the unused portion. On 2026-09-09 PBF Energy Company LLC closed the purchase of two hydrogen plants at the Torrance refinery from Air Products and contributed them to the issuer, which recognised USD 388.4 million of property, plant and equipment and removed an operating lease liability of USD 139.7 million and a right-of-use asset of USD 140.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the balance-sheet date, on 2026-10-26, the issuer redeemed all USD 800.0 million of its 9.875% notes due 2030 at 106.67% of principal, about USD 853.4 million, from cash on hand; a loss of USD 70.4 million is to be booked in Q4 2026. PBF Energy declared a dividend of USD 0.325 per share on 2026-10-29, payable on 2026-11-24, and the issuer may need to distribute cash to PBF Energy Company LLC to fund it. PBF Energy must file a resale registration statement for the exchange shares by 2026-12-31 or special interest of 0.25% to 0.50% a year accrues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level rests on mixed behaviour: net outflows to the parent in FY2023 and FY2024, support in FY2025 and 2026, creditor-aligned refinancing and no documented liability management. Countervailing evidence is the 2026 net contributions and redemptions at a premium. Further analysis needs the executed debt documents and the parent's proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PBF Holding Co LLC (issuer id pbf-holding-co-llc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: the fundamental credit profile of the issuer, its strongest support, its weakest dimension, its primary downside path and what to monitor, on the issuer's own statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PBF Holding is a strong credit today but a cyclical one: net cash and 0.40x leverage rest on refining margins far above the loss-making FY2024 and FY2025 levels, so creditors are protected by liquidity more than by earnings. Net cash was USD 897.6 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 827.2 million pro forma for the redemption of the last 2030 notes on 2026-10-26.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CB1; calculation CB2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After that redemption no drawn debt matures before 2032 and the revolver is undrawn, so the primary downside path is a return to FY2025 margins that turns cash flow negative while capital spending and parent distributions continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CB5; calculation CB6; calculation CB9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and low leverage are the main support, and no drawn debt falls due before 2032 once the October redemption is counted. Debt was 0.40x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 6.90x at FY2025, cash interest was covered 25.09x against 2.05x, and revolver availability was about USD 3,100.0 million after the commitment was raised to USD 4.0 billion and extended to 2031-09-30. After the October redemption USD 1,050.0 million of notes remain, due in 2032 and 2034.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation CB1; calculation CB3; calculation CB9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are the weak point because they follow the refining cycle. EBITDA excluding special items was negative USD 124.2 million in FY2024 and negative USD 9.5 million in FY2025, when gross refining margin was USD 7.89 and USD 8.77 per barrel, against USD 3,259.1 million for the first nine months of 2026 at USD 22.96 per barrel. Each USD 1.00 per barrel of margin is worth about USD 304.0 million a year at FY2025 volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation CB4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow in 2026 is strong but not all earned. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 3,070.6 million and capital spending USD 933.8 million, but accrued expenses added USD 981.1 million while receivables absorbed USD 904.3 million and inventories USD 339.0 million. Inventory-related accruals rose to USD 2,378.3 million from USD 1,351.5 million at 2025-12-31 and the filings do not say what they are owed to, and USD 102.9 million of operating cash flow was insurance proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation CB8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing risk is low until 2032, but market access has been shown at the top of the cycle and at a high price in the trough. The 2034 notes of USD 500.0 million at 7.25% and the 2032 exchangeable notes of USD 550.0 million were placed in 2026, and annual cash coupons fell from about USD 166.5 million to USD 36.25 million, yet in March 2025, a loss year, the issuer paid a coupon close to ten percent to place USD 800.0 million of 2030 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17-18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21-22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation CB10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin resilience is weak because product and crude prices are set by the market and regulatory cost is large. Renewable fuel compliance cost rose to USD 1,132.1 million for nine months from USD 454.0 million, though it took 19.31% of reported gross refining margin against 25.90% a year earlier, and a change of USD 1.00 per MMBTU in natural gas moves annual energy cost by USD 70.0 million to USD 100.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation CB12; calculation CB15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital spending is the main lever in a downturn, and it has limits. Turnarounds were 32.68% of nine-month capital spending, the 2026 guidance is USD 825.0 million to USD 875.0 million excluding the Martinez rebuild with two turnarounds moved to 2027, and FY2025 spending was USD 1,144.0 million; deferring maintenance saves cash but raises outage risk at a system with one reportable segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66-67; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156; calculation CB8; calculation CB13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Structure and the parent are a second downside channel. The notes rank behind a USD 4.0 billion secured revolver and behind subsidiaries that do not guarantee them, and net cash flows to the parent were outflows of USD 424.0 million in FY2023 and USD 306.0 million in FY2024 before turning into net contributions of USD 199.6 million in FY2025 and USD 29.6 million in the first nine months of 2026; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation CB11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Event risk and information gaps cap confidence. Penalties from the Martinez fire investigations are unknown although insurers have paid USD 1.25 billion, the effect of the Chalmette fire of 2026-05-08 is not stated, and no current ratings, peer data, covenant calculations or management forecast are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence that the credit is stronger than a cyclical reading allows is the size of the buffer: pro forma net cash of USD 827.2 million plus revolver availability of about USD 3,100.0 million would cover about 2.21 years of cash burn at the FY2025 rate before insurance, adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months was USD 3,505.2 million, and annual cash coupons have fallen by about USD 130.2 million. The view would move to a stronger one if gross refining margin per barrel stays well above the FY2025 level for several more quarters while the inventory-related accruals do not reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CB1; calculation CB2; calculation CB6; calculation CB7; calculation CB10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a weaker view is that two of the last three years lost money at the EBITDA level before special items, that the 2026 margin is more than two and a half times the FY2025 margin, and that at the FY2025 margin nine-month adjusted EBITDA would have been negative USD 145.4 million on the same volumes. Gross refining margin per barrel below USD 10.00 for two quarters, a revolver draw, or a distribution to the parent above its dividend need would move the view to weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation CB5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside figures apply FY2025 margins to 2026 volumes and hold costs and working capital constant, so the swing in adjusted EBITDA and the 2.21-year cover are scale illustrations and not forecasts; costs, the revolver borrowing base and parent distributions would all move, and the downside conclusion could be better or worse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CB5; calculation CB6; calculation CB7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer financials, market prices or current ratings are supplied, so the claim that margins are cyclical rests on this issuer's own FY2023 to FY2026 history and the comparison with other leveraged refiners is not established; a peer set could change the business profile conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management forecast or forward model is supplied, so the outlook beyond the parent's fourth-quarter throughput guidance and the 2026 capital guidance is not established; a forecast could change the medium-term conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strengths are liquidity, distant and cheaper debt, scale, recovered interest cover and insurance recoveries already received. Net cash and about USD 3,100.0 million of revolver availability sit against USD 1,050.0 million of notes due in 2032 and 2034 after the October redemption, and annual cash coupons fell by about USD 130.2 million; the issuer runs six refineries in four regions with a weighted-average Nelson Complexity Index of 12.8; interest cover was 25.09x; and insurers have paid USD 1.25 billion of the Martinez claim, which management expects to finalise before year-end 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation CB1; calculation CB9; calculation CB10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are cyclical earnings, cash-flow quality, regulatory cost, cash calls from the parent and ranking. EBITDA excluding special items was negative in FY2024 and FY2025; 2026 operating cash flow leans on accruals and insurance; renewable fuel compliance cost reached USD 1,132.1 million for nine months; parent distributions were USD 156.4 million for nine months with an 18% dividend increase declared; and the notes sit behind a USD 4.0 billion secured revolver and non-guarantor subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation CB4; calculation CB8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PBF Holding is a wholly owned subsidiary of a listed parent and owns six refineries in four regions, with about one million barrels a day of capacity and one reportable segment. The parent controls it through a direct owner, the three directors are the parent's executives, and no financial sponsor is named, so exit pressure does not apply; the chain of control and the parent's claim on issuer cash are the governance facts that matter to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows product prices and volumes rather than contracts: most sales are spot or short-term, gasoline and distillates are 88.82% of nine-month revenue, and one customer is about 13% of FY2025 revenue. Revenue fell 23.48% from FY2023 to FY2025 and gross refining margin per barrel excluding special items fell from USD 16.07 to USD 8.77, or 45.43%, while EBITDA excluding special items fell from USD 2,357.6 million to negative USD 9.5 million, so a modest fall in revenue and a margin cut of less than half removed all of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CB14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are largely fixed at the refinery level: operating expenses were USD 2,581.3 million, USD 2,487.8 million and USD 2,547.0 million in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 while throughput fell, and operating expense per barrel was USD 8.15 for nine months of 2026. Energy is the main variable cost, about half the workforce is under collective bargaining agreements, and renewable fuel compliance and general expenses rose in 2026. Capital intensity is high, with capital and turnaround spending of USD 1,144.0 million in FY2025 and USD 933.8 million for nine months of 2026, so free cash flow depends on margin and on how much turnaround work is deferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is intense and sets margins: the issuer competes with integrated oil companies and foreign refiners, some larger and with their own crude, while it buys crude and feedstocks from unaffiliated suppliers. Customers are not concentrated beyond one buyer at about 13% of revenue and most volume is sold at market prices, so neither buyer nor supplier power is the main risk; substitutes matter through renewable fuel mandates and energy transition policy, which raise compliance cost and could erode product demand over time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and geopolitics are material to credit. The March 2026 federal renewable fuel rule raised compliance cost, the issuer intends to defer settlement of its California emissions obligation until 2029, and the issuer says hostilities involving the United States, Israel, the Gulf States and Iran lifted refining margins and working capital needs while their duration is uncertain. Other macro, social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are liquidity, distant maturities, scale and recovered cover; the weaknesses are cyclical margins, cash flow that leans on accruals and insurance, regulatory cost and ranking behind secured debt. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are the cost programme, which management says should reach more than USD 350 million of run-rate savings by year-end 2026, and a lasting margin level; the threats are margin normalisation, penalties from the Martinez investigations and parent cash calls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_a991pressreleaseq3-26.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions of the financial profile the assessment is: scale and market position strong on capacity and complexity but not compared with peers; competitive advantage average, from coastal complexity without proprietary crude; business diversification average, with four regions but one product slate; cost and capex flexibility average, with turnarounds deferrable within limits; margin stability weak; free cash flow stability weak, with negative operating cash flow in FY2024 and FY2025; ability to refinance average, because access came at a near double-digit coupon in 2025; liquidity strong; and financial policy and governance average, in line with the medium sponsor risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the near-term drivers are the margin level, the renewable fuel compliance cost, the finalisation of the Martinez claim expected before year-end 2026, the 2027 catch-up of deferred turnarounds and the parent's dividend, which management raised by 18%. The tailwinds are wide spreads, lower interest cost and no maturity before 2032; the headwinds are margin normalisation, working capital reversal and regulatory penalties. No medium-term forecast is supplied, so the three-to-five-year outlook is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66-68; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_a991pressreleaseq3-26.htm.jsonl, pages 1-3; calculation CB10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a normalisation of crack spreads from the Q3 2026 level toward the FY2025 level while renewable fuel compliance cost stays high. The first operational break is gross refining margin per barrel falling to the FY2025 level of USD 8.77: on nine-month volumes that removes about USD 3,429.7 million of margin and would turn nine-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,284.3 million to about negative USD 145.4 million, holding costs constant. Operating cash flow turns negative as it did in FY2024 and FY2025, and the accrued liabilities that rose in 2026 would be a further call on cash if they unwind.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pbf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation CB5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At the FY2025 cash burn of USD 1,778.9 million before insurance, pro forma net cash of USD 827.2 million plus revolver availability of about USD 3,100.0 million would cover roughly 2.21 years, with no maturity before 2032. Management levers are deferring turnarounds, which were 32.68% of nine-month capital spending, cutting the cost programme further and limiting parent distributions, which are discretionary apart from tax distributions. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next two years, but the revolver borrowing base would shrink as prices fall, and the observable trigger is gross refining margin per barrel below USD 10.00 for two quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_pbfh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CB6; calculation CB7; calculation CB13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, PBF Holding presents a business profile that is large and complex but fully exposed to the refining cycle, supported by net cash, a distant maturity profile and revolver availability of about USD 3,100.0 million, but credit quality is constrained by cyclical margins, cash-flow quality, regulatory cost and cash calls from the parent. Cash-flow durability is weak at FY2025 margins and strong at 2026 margins. Refinancing capacity depends on the margin cycle and on the revolver borrowing base, and the primary downside path is a margin reversal that burns cash while capital spending and distributions continue. A more definitive opinion would need the executed debt documents, current ratings, peer data and a forecast. Top risk: refining margin reversal.
